newsitem.title: THAILAND: New Aspiration ahead of Democrats in Thai poll-TV.
newsitem.headline: New Aspiration ahead of Democrats in Thai poll-TV.

text.p: The New Aspiration Party (NAP) of Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh moved past the Democrat Party in unofficial television and radio projections of the result in Sunday's Thai elections.

Official Radio Thailand and the Channel 7 television station put the NAP slightly ahead of the Democrat Party of former premier Chuan Leekpai. Earlier three television stations had given the Democrat Party the edge over the NAP.
Radio Thailand projected the NAP would win 127 seats in the 393-seat parliament against 124 for the the Democrats based on vote counts about 4-1/2 hours after polling ended at 0800 GMT.
Channel 7 television gave the NAP 125 and the Democrats 124 seats but Channel 9 said the NAP was set to win 125 seats to the Democrats 126.

The NAP and the Democrats were seen running neck and neck even before polling closed in the Thai election, which is the fourth in four years and said by analysts to be the most violent and dirty in two decades. The leaders of the parties were unavailable for comment.

The election watchdog Pollwatch said seven people had been killed in election-related violence since the campaign began and up to 30 billion baht ($1.2 billion) had been spent by politicians on campaigns and vote-buying.
